 Magnitude 3.4 earthquake strikes near Huntsville, felt in Weber and Davis counties
 By Gephardt Daily Staff - November 14, 2026 
 Facebook X Pinterest WhatsApp 
 Map: University of Utah Seismograph Stations 
 HUNTSVILLE, Utah, Nov. 14, 2026 (Gephardt Daily) — A magnitude 3.4 earthquake struck about 7 miles northwest of Huntsville on Saturday night, prompting reports of shaking from residents in Weber and Davis counties.
 The earthquake occurred at 6:40 p.m., according to the University of Utah Seismograph Stations, which classified it as a minor quake.
 More than 310 reports of people feeling the earthquake had been received by 9:15 p.m. 
 The Utah Division of Emergency Management said in a social media update that it was hearing from people who felt the quake in Ogden, east Layton and Syracuse, and as far south as Fruit Heights.
 The division credited university seismologists with refining the epicenter’s location and noted that an earthquake of that magnitude can go unnoticed, even by people living nearby.
 Since 1981, the University of Utah Seismograph Stations has located 73 earthquakes of magnitude 2 or greater within 15 miles of Saturday’s epicenter. The largest was a magnitude 3.7 earthquake on Aug. 30, 2023, according to the university.
